prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: In frames 1 to 4, the depth map shows the camera wearer looking straight down at a flat ironing table (~0.6–0.8 m away) with their own torso at the bottom edge (~0.3–0.4 m) and both forearms extending forward within arm's reach (~0.4–0.6 m) over a folded cloth and a raised iron on the right (~0.5–0.7 m). Across frames 1 to 4, the brighter right arm shifts from ~0.15 m beside the left hand on the left to ~0.5 m away on the right to grasp and slide the iron, occluding the garment and table beneath them while the background floor drops off into dark regions (>1.2 m) around the table's edges. In frame 5, the viewpoint turns left away from the table (partially visible as a bright region at the bottom-right at ~0.7–0.9 m), looking across the darker floor (~1.3–1.8 m) toward a second person seated ~1.5–2.0 m away in the upper-left (~1.3 m from the table), who faces roughly toward the camera wearer with their head and upper shoulders cropped out of the top frame edge and their hands together in their lap (~0.3 m from their torso, well out of the wearer's reach). Compared to the RGB strip alone, the depth map clearly separates the elevated table plane and overhanging cloth on the top-left of frame 1 from the recessed floor and captures the raised 3D profile of the iron and arms above the surface. However, the map is unreliable in maintaining consistent absolute depth scale across frames—over-saturating the wearer's skirt and the table corner in frame 5—and it merges thin structures like the iron's power cord into the flat tabletop.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map isolates foreground regions of the camera wearer ('person' masks at ~0.3–0.7 m at the bottom) in frames 1 to 4 and detects the seated second person ('person' masks at ~1.5–2.0 m in the upper-left) in frame 5, while leaving the surrounding room layout, floor (~1.3–1.8 m), and ironing board mostly unmasked black background. Across frames 1 to 4, the wearer's masked arms reach forward over the table within arm's reach (~0.4–0.6 m) and separate from ~0.15 m to ~0.5 m as the right hand grasps and moves the iron on the right, before the camera turns left in frame 5 where the wearer's lower torso and left arm sit at the bottom-left (~0.4–0.6 m) roughly 1.2–1.5 m away from the seated person facing them with an occluded upper body and hands in their lap. Although the masks help distinguish the human figures and the held appliance in frame 3 from the busy floral tablecloth and patterned floor in the RGB images, the segmentation map is highly unreliable for scene geometry and object identity. It completely fails to segment the cloth being ironed or the iron in frames 2 and 4, mislabels the iron held in the wearer's right hand as a 'remote' (green mask at ~0.6 m) in frame 3, and misclassifies parts of the lower-right cabinet and bottom-left floor edge as a 'laptop' in frames 2 and 5. Furthermore, it bleeds the wearer's 'person' mask onto the floral tabletop and folded garment in frames 1 to 4 and fragments both the camera wearer and the seated person in frame 5 into multiple overlapping 'person' instances.
descriptions.pose: The pose map renders 2D magenta hand skeletons for the camera wearer's left and right hands within arm's reach (~0.4–0.7 m directly in front and below the viewpoint) across frames 1 to 4, while detecting no yellow body skeletons in any frame and no keypoints at all in frame 5. In frame 1, the curled left hand and open right hand lie close together (~0.15 m apart) on the left side of the table; in frame 2, the left hand moves to the lower-left edge while the right hand reaches ~0.4 m right toward the iron; and in frames 3 and 4, the flat left hand stabilizes the upper-left corner of the cloth while the right hand curls around the iron handle and slides right to a ~0.5 m separation. Compared to the RGB frames alone, the hand skeletons explicitly reveal the 21-joint finger articulation and contrast the splayed, flat posture of the left hand against the closed grasping posture of the right hand even when the iron handle and fingers partially self-occlude in frames 3 and 4. However, the pose map is unreliable for full-scene spatial understanding because it omits all arm and torso links, provides no distance or surface cues for the table or iron, and completely fails in frame 5 to detect both the camera wearer's visible left hand (~0.5 m away at the bottom-left) and the seated second person ~1.5–2.0 m away in the upper-left (who faces toward the wearer with head cropped out and hands holding a small object ~0.3 m in front of their hips).
